mainTopic: What is included when selling a חצר, and when one act of possession acquires several properties
overview: The amud opens with the end of an earlier discussion: a daughter's tenth of her father's estate was collected even from fixed millstones, and רב אשי adds that in רב כהנא's house they collected it even from rent money. Then a new משנה begins. Someone who sells a חצר sells the houses, pits, ditches and caves in it, but not the movables, unless he says 'it and everything in it.' Either way, the bathhouse and the olive press are not sold, and רבי אליעזר says only the open space of the חצר is sold. A ברייתא adds that outer and inner houses are included. Stores go with the חצר if they open into it, and the גמרא settles a contradiction with רבי חייא: a store that opens both ways goes with the חצר only if it is mostly used from inside. רבה explains that the dispute with רבי אליעזר is about what the seller's word means, and two versions of his explanation are given. Finally, רב נחמן rules that taking possession of a sand field does not acquire a pond sold with it. The גמרא defends this against שמואל's rule about ten fields: properties with different uses need separate acts of acquisition. The amud ends by opening a second version of that discussion, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Collecting the daughter's tenth even from millstones
steps.stepSummary: The tail of an earlier story: a daughter's dowry of one tenth of the estate was collected even from the fixed lower millstones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He collected for her a tenth of the estate, even from the lower millstones.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of an earlier discussion. A ruling was made that the daughter's tenth of her father's property could be collected even from the lower millstones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter's dowry is taken from land, not from movable items. Lower millstones are fixed in place, so they count like land and are included in the calculation.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of the property: the daughter's dowry share from her father's estate
The lower millstones, which are fixed into the ground
He collected it for her

phrases.english: He collected for her a tenth of the property,
phrases.notes: This finishes an earlier story about a daughter getting a tenth of her father's estate as her dowry.

phrases.english: even from the lower millstones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגְבַּהּ עִישּׂוּר נִכְסֵי, אֲפִילּוּ מֵאִצְטְרוֹבְלֵי דְרֵיחַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fixed lower millstones count as land for collecting the daughter's tenth.

steps.title: רב אשי: even rent money was included
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that in רב כהנא's study hall they collected the daughter's tenth even from the rent of houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in רב כהנא's house, we would collect even from the rent of houses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a personal report that goes one step further than the millstones. They even collected the daughter's tenth from rent money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rent is money, not land. But because it comes from houses, it was treated like land and included in the dowry calculation. This is a bigger step than the millstones, which are at least physically attached.

keyTerms.meaning: The house or study hall of רב כהנא
We would collect
The rent earned from houses

steps.whatToRemember: The daughter's tenth comes from land, and that was stretched to include fixed millstones and even rent from houses.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in Rav Kahana's house,
we would collect even from the rent of houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an even broader practice to the millstone ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rent from houses was treated like land for collecting the daughter's tenth.

steps.title: Selling a courtyard: what is included by default
steps.stepSummary: Someone who sells a חצר sells the houses, pits, ditches and caves in it, but not the movable items.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sells a courtyard has sold the houses, pits, ditches and caves, but not the movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us what automatically comes with a חצר when it is sold without details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things built into or dug into the ground count as part of the חצר and go to the buyer. Things that can be picked up and carried away are not part of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
One who sells a courtyard
Pits, ditches and caves: things dug into the ground
Movable property

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sells a courtyard –
has sold the houses, pits, ditches and caves;
but not the movable items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the dowry discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a חצר includes the attached and dug-in structures but not the movables.

steps.title: Saying 'it and everything in it' includes the movables
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says 'it and everything in it,' everything is sold, even the movable items.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he said to him, 'It and everything in it,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. With a broader wording, even the movable items go with the חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The default rule from the previous step can be widened by what the seller says. The words 'everything in it' clearly cover the movables too.

keyTerms.meaning: It and everything that is in it
All of them are sold

phrases.english: When he said to him:
'It and everything that is in it' –
all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: הוּא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a wording that widens the default sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'it and everything in it' includes the movables in the sale.

steps.title: Bathhouse and olive press are never included
steps.stepSummary: In both cases, the bathhouse and the olive press inside the חצר are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, he has not sold the bathhouse, nor the olive press that is in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit that applies to both earlier cases. The bathhouse and olive press stay with the seller even if he said 'everything in it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bathhouse and an olive press are separate businesses with their own purpose, not just parts of the חצר. So even broad wording does not include them.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way: in both cases
Bathhouse
Olive press

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'everything in it' covers everything. It covers the movables, but not separate units like the bathhouse and olive press.

phrases.english: Either way –
phrases.notes: Whether he sold it plainly or said 'it and everything in it.'

phrases.english: he has not sold the bathhouse,
nor the olive press that is in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ – לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הַמֶּרְחָץ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bathhouse and olive press are excluded from any sale of the חצר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: only the open space is sold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that selling a חצר sells only its open air space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One who sells a courtyard has sold only the airspace of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה. He says a plain sale gives the buyer only the open area, not even the houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the word 'חצר' means only the open yard. The houses, pits and caves are separate things that need to be named.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees here
The airspace or open area of the courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the משנה: built-in and dug-in parts go with the חצר, movables only with 'everything in it,' and never the bathhouse or olive press. רבי אליעזר: only the open space.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who sells a courtyard –

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא אֲוִירָהּ שֶׁל חָצֵר.
phrases.english: has sold only the airspace of the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a חצר includes only its open space.

steps.title: ברייתא: outer and inner houses are included
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that selling a חצר includes the outer houses, the inner houses and the בית החולסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sells a courtyard has sold the outer houses, the inner houses, and the בית החולסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fills in details about the houses the משנה mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not only houses that open straight onto the חצר are included. Inner houses, which you reach only through the outer ones, are included too, and so is an extra area called בית החולסאות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
Outer houses, opening directly onto the courtyard
Inner houses, reached through the outer houses
An area connected to the courtyard, often explained as a sandy area

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
One who sells a courtyard –
has sold the outer houses,
and the inner houses,
and the area of the sand fields.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details to the משנה's list of what is included.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both outer and inner houses and the בית החולסאות go with the חצר.

steps.title: ברייתא: which stores go with the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Stores that open into the חצר are sold with it, stores that don't are not, and stores that open both ways are sold with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stores that open into it are sold with it; those that do not open into it are not sold with it; those that open both ways are sold with it, like the first kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with three kinds of stores. Which way the store's door opens decides whether it goes with the חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A store opening into the חצר belongs to it, and one opening only to the street does not. A store with doors both ways is grouped with the stores that open inside, so it is sold too. This last ruling is the one the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Stores
Opening into it, into the courtyard
This way and that way: in both directions
They are sold with it

phrases.english: Stores that open into it –
are sold with it,
and those that do not open into it –
are not sold with it.
Those that open both here and there –
phrases.notes: Into the courtyard and also out to the public street.

phrases.english: [these] and those are sold with it.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets comes from the corrected wording. Both kinds of stores, inside-only and two-way, go with the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the rules for stores.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stores that open into the חצר, even if they also open outward, are sold with it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא: only the open space
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats רבי אליעזר's view using the word מילוסא for the open space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One who sells a courtyard has sold only the open space of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's disagreement, the same idea as in the משנה but with a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילוסא here means the same as אויר in the משנה: the open, empty part of the חצר. For רבי אליעזר, none of the houses or stores are included.

keyTerms.meaning: The open space of the courtyard

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who sells a courtyard –

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא מִילוּסָא שֶׁל חָצֵר.
phrases.english: has sold only the open space of the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הֶחָצֵר – לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא מִילוּסָא שֶׁל חָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the dissenting view inside the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the open space of the חצר is sold.

steps.title: רבי חייא teaches the opposite about two-way stores
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling that two-way stores are sold with the חצר and challenges it with רבי חייא's teaching that they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Stores that open both ways are sold with it. But רבי חייא taught: They are not sold with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks out the ruling about two-way stores and shows that another ברייתא, taught by רבי חייא, says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources give opposite rulings on the same case. One says two-way stores go with the חצר, and the other says they do not. The גמרא needs a way to fit both together.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: quoting the earlier source to discuss it
But didn't he teach: introduces a contradicting source
A תנא who collected ברייתות

phrases.english: The Master said:
Those that open both here and there –
are sold with it.
But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya teach:
They are not sold with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: פְּתוּחוֹת לְכָאן וּלְכָאן – נִמְכָּרוֹת עִמָּהּ. וְהָא תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last ruling about stores in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that stores opening both ways are sold with the חצר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's ברייתא rules the exact opposite on the same case.

steps.title: It depends where most of the use is
steps.stepSummary: The two sources are talking about different stores: one used mostly from inside the חצר, the other used mostly from the street.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is where most of their use is from inside, and that one is where most of their use is from outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of two-way store.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a two-way store is used mostly from inside the חצר, it goes with the חצר. That is the first ברייתא. If it is used mostly from the street, it does not, and that is רבי חייא's ברייתא. So the deciding factor is the main use, not just which way the doors open.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: introduces an answer
Most of their use
Inside, from the courtyard
Outside, from the street

steps.whatToRemember: A store that opens both into the חצר and into the street goes with the חצר only if it is mostly used from inside the חצר.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is where most of their use is inside,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the first ברייתא, which says the stores are sold.

phrases.english: that is where most of their use is outside.
phrases.notes: 'That' is רבי חייא's teaching, which says they are not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא דְּרוֹב תַּשְׁמִישְׁתַּיְיהוּ לְגוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to argue about the same two-way store.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whether the store goes with the חצר depends on whether most of its use is from inside or from outside.

steps.title: רבה explains the courtyard dispute through the seller's exact word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי אליעזר's view that selling a courtyard means only its open space. רבה explains that the argument depends on which Aramaic word the seller used: everyone agrees that 'דירתא' includes the houses, and they argue only about 'דרתא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: someone who sells the courtyard has sold only the open air of the courtyard. רבה said: if the seller said 'דירתא' (living place), everyone agrees it means the houses too. They argue when he said 'דרתא' (courtyard). One opinion holds it means only the garden area, and the other holds it means the houses too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי אליעזר's opinion so that רבה can explain what the argument is really about. רבה says the whole dispute depends on the word the seller used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה makes the argument smaller. With the word 'דירתא', which clearly means a home, no one argues that the houses are included. The dispute is only over 'דרתא': רבי אליעזר hears it as the open garden space, and the תנא קמא hears it as the whole property with its houses.

keyTerms.meaning: The open air or open space of the courtyard, not the buildings
A living place or residence, which clearly includes the houses
A courtyard; the word the two opinions argue over
A garden or open area between the houses
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: דֵּירְתָּא and דָּרְתָּא look almost the same, but they are two different words. In רבה's first version, the first one clearly includes the houses, and only the second one is argued about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who sells the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא אֲוִירָהּ שֶׁל חָצֵר.
phrases.english: has sold only the open space of the courtyard.
Rabba said:
If he said to him 'dirata' (a living place),
everyone agrees
that it means the houses.
Where they argue is when he said to him 'darta' (courtyard):
One Sage holds it means the garden area,
and the other Sage holds it means the houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה (step 6) and explains his dispute with the תנא קמא (step 3).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that 'דירתא' includes the houses. With 'דרתא', רבי אליעזר says only the garden area is sold, and the תנא קמא says the houses are included.

steps.title: A second version of רבה: the argument is over the word 'חצר'
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of רבה's words, everyone agrees that 'דרתא' includes the houses. The argument is only over the Hebrew word 'חצר': it means either just the open air, or the whole area together with its buildings, like the חצר המשכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבה said: if he said 'דרתא', everyone agrees it means the houses too. They argue when he said 'חצר'. One opinion holds 'חצר' means the open air, and the other holds it is like the courtyard of the משכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another report of what רבה said. This time the agreed word is 'דרתא' and the word in dispute is 'חצר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, 'דרתא' now clearly includes the houses. The argument moves to the word 'חצר'. רבי אליעזר takes it to mean only the open air. The תנא קמא compares it to the חצר המשכן, a courtyard that had the משכן standing inside it, so a חצר includes its buildings.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; a second version of the same teaching
Open air, empty space
The courtyard of the משכן, which had the משכן building inside it

phrases.english: Some say that Rabba said:
If he said to him 'darta',
everyone agrees
that it means the houses.
Where they argue is when he said to him 'chatzer':
One Sage holds 'chatzer' means the open air,
and the other Sage holds it is like the courtyard of the Mishkan.
phrases.notes: The משכן courtyard had the משכן standing inside it, so here a 'courtyard' includes its buildings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבה's explanation from step 12, moving the dispute one word up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that 'דרתא' includes the houses. With 'חצר', רבי אליעזר says only the open air is sold, and the תנא קמא says the buildings are included, like the חצר המשכן.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of רבה, the argument between רבי אליעזר and the תנא קמא is about what a word means. In each version, one clear word includes the houses for everyone, and only the less clear word is in dispute.

steps.title: Buying a sand field and a pond: taking possession of one does not acquire the other
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב נחמן: if someone sold a sand field and a pond together, the buyer's act of taking possession of one does not acquire the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב נחמן: if someone sold another person a sand field and a pond, and the buyer took possession of the sand field, he did not acquire the pond. If he took possession of the pond, he did not acquire the sand field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about acquiring property. When two pieces of land are sold together, a קנין done on one does not work for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, one act of חזקה can acquire several properties that are sold together. רב נחמן says this does not work for a חולסית and a מצולה. The buyer has to do a separate act of acquisition for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandy field, used for its sand
A pond or deep water area
He took possession through an act of חזקה, such as working or improving the land
He acquired; the sale is final

phrases.english: And Rabba said that Rav Nachman said:
If he sold him a sand field and a pond,
and he took possession of the sand field, he did not acquire the pond;
if he took possession of the pond, he did not acquire the sand field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from רבה, likely placed here because the earlier ברייתא in step 7 mentioned the בית החולסאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking possession of a sand field does not acquire a pond sold together with it, and taking possession of the pond does not acquire the sand field.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל: one field acquires ten fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן's rule can be true, since שמואל rules that if ten fields in ten different places are sold together, taking possession of one acquires all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But שמואל said: if someone sold another person ten fields in ten different regions, once the buyer took possession of one of them, he acquired all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's rule. It quotes שמואל, who holds that one act of possession can acquire many separate properties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one חזקה works even for ten fields spread across ten regions, it should surely work for a sand field and a pond sold together. So שמואל's rule seems to contradict רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
But didn't someone say; brings a source that contradicts
Regions, separate places

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שָׂדוֹת בְּעֶשֶׂר מְדִינוֹת,
phrases.english: If he sold him ten fields in ten regions,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהֶחְזִיק בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן – קָנָה כּוּלָּן!
phrases.english: once he took possession of one of them, he acquired them all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that taking possession of the sand field does not acquire the pond.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one חזקה acquires ten fields that are far apart, it should also acquire a sand field and a pond sold together.

steps.title: Same kind of land versus different uses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ten fields are all the same kind of land with one use, farming. The sand field and the pond each have a different use, so one cannot acquire the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is all one kind of land, and all of it has one use. But here, this one has its own use, and that one has its own use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing how the two cases are different. The deciding factor is whether the properties are used the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Distance does not matter. What matters is whether the properties are one type with one use. The ten fields are all farmland, so they count as one unit. A sand field and a pond are used for different things, so each one needs its own קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here; used to compare two cases
The block or body of the land; all land counts as one connected block
Use, purpose
Separate, on its own

steps.whatToRemember: One act of חזקה can acquire several properties sold together, even if they are far apart, as long as they have the same use. Properties with different uses, like a sand field and a pond, each need their own act of acquisition.
steps.confusionAlert: The difference is not about distance. The ten fields are in ten different regions and still go together. The test is whether the properties share the same use.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּסַדָּנָא דְאַרְעָא חַד הוּא,
phrases.english: There, it is because the land is all one block,
and all of it has one use;
but here,
this one has its own use,
and that one has its own use.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הוּא דְּסַדָּנָא דְאַרְעָא חַד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 and keeps רב נחמן's rule from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: one use versus separate uses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one חזקה works for ten distant fields, it should work for any properties sold together.
steps.terutzMaskana: One חזקה works only for properties with the same use. Fields with one use go together; a sand field and a pond do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule for acquiring land: properties that share one use can be acquired together with one act, while properties with different uses need separate acts of acquisition.

steps.title: Introducing a second version of the discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא signals that it is about to give another version of the discussion it just finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say a different version:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is not making a new point yet. It is setting up the next move by telling us that another version of the previous discussion is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי' mean the teaching was passed down in two forms. The version we just learned is not thrown out. The second version comes next, and we compare the two once we see it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say': this opens a second version of a teaching
'There is' or 'there are'
'Who say'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this line argues with the previous step or rejects it. It only tells us that the same discussion was passed down in another form.
